new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed, so the spot-check was on that work. copies we hold: nothing missed. Body pages not yet obtained, spot-checked through the IA full-text index (be-api.us.archive.org/fts/v1/search, identifier:californiaindian0000goll; results saved as in the okwa1235 directory): 'Okwanuchu AND (stress OR accent OR pitch)' and 'Okwanuchu AND phonolog' return no Okwanuchu-specific passage. The only stress sentence the index surfaces is the Hokan-phylum generalisation in §3.8, '(i, e, a, o, u) both short and long. Stress patterns vary from language to language, and pitch accent has developed (apparently separately) in Northern Pomo..', and the §3.11 phonology paragraph opens 'Shasta has…

sources.citation: Zhivlov, Mikhail (comp.). 2012. Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Shastan group (Hokan family). Global Lexicostatistical Database, Moscow (text version of database created 18/12/2012; main source Silver 1961 SCIL vocabulary, plus Bright & Olmsted 1959, Silver 1964/1966/1980, McLendon 1964).
sources.note: Nothing about Okwanuchu (language not included). For Shasta proper it only explains the transliteration of Silver's transcription into the GLD's unified system; a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/pitch/tone in the text finds no prosodic statement either. downloaded through slot8 after the disk gate (332 KB), extracted text; PDF deleted, text kept in the work directory, not placed in the okwa1235 mirror because it is not about this languoid.

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. & A. L. Kroeber. 1903. The Native Languages of California. American Anthropologist n.s. 5(1): 1-26.
sources.note: nothing on accent; Shasta grouped phonetically with the 'somewhat rough' Achomawi and morphologically with the northern incorporating languages

sources.citation: C. Hart Merriam papers relating to work with California Indians (Bancroft Library, BANC FILM 1556), reel 111 (ethnosynonymy cards), reel 33 'Vocabularies' (= Golla Appendix A G/6d/V22, 'O-kwahn-noo-choo-hish', Lottie O'Neal and Rose Ryan, Squaw Creek & Upper McCloud, 1925), reel 53 'Natural History Word Lists'.
sources.note: Reel 111 cards 'Okwanuchu' (copied from Handbook of American Indians pt.2 p.117, 1910: language 'in part close to that of the Shasta proper, but it contains a number of totally distinct words') and 'Oo-kwah-noo-tsoo' (Wintoon informant 1928). Reel 33 holds the handwritten 1925 vocabulary schedule but its scanned is unusable (no hit for 'kwahn'); it is a word list and cannot contain a stress statement. Reel 53 scanned has no Okwanuchu hit.

sources.citation: Survey of California and Other Indian Languages / California Language Archive. 'Okwanuchu' language page and CLA item list (langid 254).
sources.note: 'Our only information about this language comes from fewer than 100 words recorded early in the 20th century.' CLA holds no archival items for Okwanuchu; further reading = Golla 2011 only.

sources.citation: Golla, Victor. 2011. California Indian Languages. Berkeley: University of California Press, §3.11.5 Okwanuchu, pp. 94-95.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011 FOLIO; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011) (also lendable online at archive.org; also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011 FOLIO; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM501.C2 G65 2011
sources.note: Authoritative survey of the attestation; confirms via snippets that only word lists exist. Full page needed to close the record (reads as classification/vocabulary discussion, no phonology).

sources.citation: Oswalt, Robert L. 1977. The Hokan word for 'tongue': the Pomo evidence. In: Redden, James E. (ed.), Proceedings of the 1976 Hokan-Yuman Languages Workshop (University Museum Studies 11). Carbondale: Southern Illinois University. (ERIC microfiche, archive.org micro_IA41153504_0092)
sources.note: No Okwanuchu phonology; single citation of a form. Text read around the mention, then discarded (not kept).

sources.citation: Haas, Mary R. 1963. Shasta and Proto-Hokan. Language 39(1): 40-59.
sources.note: Uses Merriam's 1925 Okwanuchu vocabulary and Dixon's forms in comparative Hokan phonology; the one linguistic paper that handled the Okwanuchu material directly. Snippets show no stress statement.

sources.citation: Bright, William & D. L. Olmsted. 1959. A Shasta vocabulary. Kroeber Anthropological Society Papers 20: 1-55.
sources.note: Shasta proper (shas1239), not Okwanuchu: phoneme inventory lists 'High pitch accent' for Shasta; Okwanuchu appears only as a group name ('okwanuchu K280, okwanuchu Cu, okwanutsu M'). Nothing on Okwanuchu stress.

sources.citation: Du Bois, Cora. 1935. Wintu Ethnography. University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 36(1): 1-148. Berkeley: University of California Press. ['Waimuk (north inhabitant?)' subarea, p. 8.]
sources.note: Nothing. Six words printed without accent marks (atsa 'water', katisuk 'bring', au-u 'wood', weri kinuni a curse word, tcuk 'sick 'em', waurantitau 'short-man'); the book's only transcription note (p.3) explains three symbols for Wintu. Whole PDF text a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/acute: no linguistic hit.

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1925. Handbook of the Indians of California (BAE Bulletin 78), 'Shastan groups' pp. 279-284; 'The Okwanuchu' p. 284.
sources.note: p.284: 'The dialect is peculiar. Many words are practically pure Shasta; others are distorted to the very verge of recognizability, or utterly different.' Ethnographic; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Merriam, C. Hart. 1925. [Okwanuchu natural-history word list] 'Field Check Lists, Pacific Coast Region: O-kwahn'-noo-choo', locality Upper McCloud River & Squaw Creek, Oct. 3-4, 1925, recorded by C. Hart Merriam ('Original'). Library of Congress, C. Hart Merriam Papers (MSS32698), Box 34, Folder 7: 'Indian vocabularies; Shastan; Okwah'noochu / O-kwahn'-noo-choo (Okwanuchu Shasta)'. 109 images.
sources.note: Word list only: printed USDA Biological Survey animal/plant schedule with handwritten Okwanuchu names, syllabified with hyphens and an acute after the accented syllable (schedule p.2: Hoo-se'-wah 'mink', Te-rech'-kik 'bat', Wah-tah'-kah 'elk', Ah-rah-ge'-yu 'deer', Ka-wahn-ge 'big', Ah-rah'-ge 'blacktail deer'). Accent MARKS are data, not a statement; no prose about accent seen on the pages viewed (1-5 of 109).

sources.citation: Merriam, C. Hart. 1925. Vocabulary of O-kwahn-noo-choo-hish (Okwanuchu), Squaw Creek & Upper McCloud River, from Lottie O'Neal and Rose Ryan. Bancroft Library, C. Hart Merriam papers, BANC FILM 1556 reel 33 (Golla Appendix A: G/6d/V22).
sources.note: The largest body of Okwanuchu data (c. 75 words, Merriam's orthography marks stressed syllables with an acute); the only place stress placement could be inferred from data. Handwritten schedule; scanned useless, 144 MB PDF not downloaded.

sources.citation: Sapir, Edward. 1917. The position of Yana in the Hokan stock. University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 13(1): 1-34.
sources.note: Nothing on accent. Cites Okwanuchu forms without accent marks in cognate sets: itsiwi 'to sleep', atsanihu 'sugar pine', axta 'blood', innux 'head', isi-; provenance table p.2: Shasta forms marked (K) from Kroeber's manuscript material.

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1907. Linguistic relationships within the Shasta-Achomawi stock. In: Congrès International des Américanistes, XVe session tenue à Québec en 1906, tome II, pp. 255-263. Québec: Dussault & Proulx.
sources.note: No accent/stress content. Gives lexical agreement percentages (Achomawi-Atsugewi ~35%, Shasta ~15%, New River <8%, Konomihu 6 of ~70 words), regular sound correspondences (Achomawi L, P, M, W : Atsugewi N, K, R, P; lax : nax 'head'), 'general phonetic character' of Konomihu 'very similar to the Shasta', and pronoun/verb morphology for Achomawi, Atsugewi, Shasta. Okwanutcu only named as a Shasta dialect.

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1907. The Shasta. Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 17(5): 381-498.
sources.note: No phonology content for Okwanuchu (no language section at all; Konomihu word list in the appendix only).

sources.citation: Dixon, Roland B. 1905. The Shasta-Achomawi: a new linguistic stock, with four new dialects. American Anthropologist n.s. 7(2): 213-217.
sources.note: Only published primary Okwanuchu data: seven words in the comparative table pp.216 (in'nux 'head', is'sawak 'ear', axta' 'blood', at'sa 'water', itu'ri 'salmon'..) carrying accent marks after the stressed syllable, plus p.215 'the general phonetic character of the Okwa'nuchu differs quite a little in some points from the Shasta, particularly in its fondness for nasals'. No statement about stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid okwa1235; Wikipedia 'Okwanuchu language'.
sources.note: Glottolog lists a single reference (Golla 2011, a wordlist or less). Wikipedia cites Golla 2011:90-91, Du Bois 1935 (a few Waymaq words, e.g. atsa 'water') and Curtin 1884 ('Wailaki on McCloud', 18 words). No phonological description exists.
